1.title: Know the words and the ways to sell online
1.intro: Selling online means a buyer finds, pays and receives a product without meeting you. Start with the basics.
pts: Learn the terms: listing, SKU, stock, shipping, returns, fees, checkout, marketplace, own store.
An online marketplace lends you its buyers; an own store gives you control but you bring the buyers.
Name one buyer in one line: who, what they need, what they worry about.
Search ten listings of a product and note price, photos and delivery time.
Compare marketplace and own-store fees for the same item.
Describe the buyer's path: search, compare, trust, pay, wait, receive.
List what a buyer cannot check online, such as size and feel, and how your listing answers it.
1.ex: Product: handmade candles. Buyer: a gift shopper who wants a clear scent, fast delivery and easy returns. Of ten listings you read, 5 promise delivery in 3 days or less, so 5 / 10 = 50 percent, and you decide to promise it too.
1.act: Compare ten listings in a table and write a buyer profile.
1.std: Task: study ten listings. Condition: public pages. Standard: table complete and buyer fits one line.

2.title: Explain how an order moves from click to delivery
2.intro: An order has steps. If you can name them, you avoid late or lost parcels.
pts: The steps: order, payment, pick, pack, ship, track, deliver, support, return.
Know your handling time and tell buyers a delivery window.
Keep a stock count that updates after each sale.
Write what you do when an item is lost or damaged.
Set a cut-off time for same-day packing and state it in the listing.
Choose tracked shipping for parcels over a set value and write the value.
Keep spare packing material so a rush of orders does not delay shipping.
2.ex: A buyer orders at 2 p.m. You pack by 5 p.m., ship the next day and send the tracking number. If handling takes 1 day and the carrier takes 3 to 5 days, you tell the buyer 4 to 6 days (1 + 3 to 1 + 5).
2.act: Draw an order flow for your product with a time and an owner for each step.
2.std: Task: map the order flow. Condition: one page. Standard: every step has an owner, a time and a record.

3.title: Create a clear listing and photos
3.intro: Now you apply the basics. Make a listing that is honest and easy to buy from.
pts: Title: say what it is, size, colour and material in plain words.
Take photos in good light from several sides, and show the real item.
Describe condition, size, weight and care. State delivery cost and time.
Do not use claims you cannot prove.
Add a scale photo of the item beside a common object.
Include the weight and box size so shipping is priced right.
Check that your first photo is clear on a small phone screen.
3.ex: Before: 'Amazing candle!!' After: 'Soy wax candle, 200 g, cedar scent, burns about 40 hours.' If you burn it 5 hours an evening, 40 / 5 = 8 evenings, which you can state once you have tested it.
3.act: Create three listings with five photos each and edit each once.
3.std: Task: write three listings. Condition: from real products. Standard: all facts true and checkable, price and delivery stated.

4.title: Follow Canadian selling rules
4.intro: Consumer, tax and product rules apply when you sell online in Canada. Learn which ones touch you.
pts: Consumer protection is mostly provincial: refunds, warranties and price display differ by province.
Collect and remit sales tax once you pass the small-supplier limit; check the current limit with the tax agency.
Some goods have label, bilingual and safety rules, especially for children and food; check the current rules.
Sell only goods you have the right to sell. Check the marketplace's own seller rules.
Write a shipping and return page in plain words.
Check whether your products need ingredient, material or origin labels; check the current rule.
Keep sales records and receipts for the period the tax agency requires.
4.ex: A buyer asks for a refund on a faulty item. You check your stated return rule and your province's rule, then respond in writing within a day. You keep the reply and the order number in one folder.
4.act: Make a table of rule, who sets it, what you must do and where you checked, for ten items.
4.std: Task: build a rules table. Condition: from official public pages. Standard: each row has a dated source; unknowns say 'check the current rule with the local authority'.

5.title: Price products and check it pays
5.intro: Price covers the product, fees, shipping and your time. Work the numbers for each item.
pts: Landed cost = item cost + shipping in + packaging.
Fees: marketplace fee, payment fee, ads. Subtract them from the sale price.
Margin = (price - all costs) / price.
Test a price rise of 10 percent and see if sales hold.
Add every cost to one sheet, one row per product.
Find the lowest price that still gives the margin you want.
Decide whether to show shipping separately or build it into the price.
5.ex: Item costs 12, packaging 1.50, fees 5 and shipping paid by you 8, so total cost = 12 + 1.50 + 5 + 8 = 26.50. At a sale price of 48, profit = 48 - 26.50 = 21.50, and margin = 21.50 / 48 = about 45 percent. Teaching figures only.
5.act: Build a price sheet for ten items with all costs and margin.
5.std: Task: compute profit per order. Condition: with a spreadsheet. Standard: every cost shown and a mentor can follow the numbers.

6.title: Get found and win trust
6.intro: Buyers buy from sellers they trust. Build a steady way to be found.
pts: Use the words buyers type in your titles and descriptions.
Answer questions within one working day.
Ask satisfied buyers for honest reviews; never buy or write fake reviews.
Use consent when you collect emails; follow Canada's anti-spam rules.
Write answers to the five most common questions and place them in the listing.
Keep a list of the words buyers use in messages and reuse them in titles.
Track the share of visitors who buy and write the number.
6.ex: A buyer asks about size. You reply with measurements and a photo beside a coin. They order and leave a review. If 200 visitors give 6 orders, 6 / 200 = 3 percent buy.
6.act: Run a four-week test: list, answer, ship and ask for reviews. Log sales and replies.
6.std: Task: run a four-week test. Condition: real listings. Standard: log complete with sales, response time and one lesson.

7.title: Protect buyers, data and money
7.intro: Care for buyer data, payments and stock builds a lasting shop.
pts: Use the platform's secure checkout; never ask for card details by message.
Keep buyer addresses private and delete what you no longer need.
Watch for fake orders, chargebacks and overpayment scams.
Check recalls and safety for goods, especially used or imported items.
Check the platform's payment rules before you ship a high-value order.
Photograph each parcel before it ships to answer damage claims.
Limit who can sign in to your seller account and review the list monthly.
7.ex: A buyer offers to overpay and asks you to return the difference. You refuse and report it to the platform. Refunding an extra 30 from a payment that later fails would cost you 30 dollars.
7.act: Write a returns policy, a privacy note and a scam checklist (one page each).
7.std: Task: write three documents. Condition: reviewed by a mentor. Standard: each is in plain words and dated.

8.title: Run a real pilot and decide
8.intro: Now you run it for real. Sell, measure and decide how to grow.
pts: Set a 60-day goal, such as 30 orders and a 30 percent margin.
Every week record orders, profit, returns, late parcels and questions.
Ask five buyers what to improve.
At the end choose: stop, change or grow, and write a 12-month plan.
Pick the one number you will improve most: orders, margin or returns.
Photograph your packing station and note what slows you down.
Hold a short review each week and write one decision.
8.ex: After 60 days: 34 orders, profit 920 dollars, 2 returns. 920 / 34 = about 27 dollars per order, and 2 / 34 is about 6 percent returns. You decide to drop the slowest product and raise one price.
8.act: Run the pilot, keep the weekly log and present a 12-month plan to a panel of three.
8.std: Task: run a 60-day pilot. Condition: real products and buyers. Standard: log complete, decision uses numbers, a panel can repeat the plan.

quiz: What is a listing?
A page that shows a product, price and details for buyers.
What does a marketplace give you?
Access to its buyers, for a fee.
What are the steps of an order?
Order, pay, pick, pack, ship, track, deliver, support, return.
What should a listing never include?
Claims you cannot prove.
How do you compute margin?
Price minus all costs, divided by price.
When must you collect sales tax?
Once you pass the small-supplier limit or choose to register; check the current rule.
Why not ask for card details by message?
It is unsafe; use the secure checkout.
How do you earn good reviews?
Ship as promised, answer fast and ask honestly; never fake them.
What do you do with used goods?
Check recalls and safety rules before selling.
What do you do when unsure about a rule?
Check the current rule with the local authority and keep the answer in writing.
